### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | Journal-specific author guidelines (Section 10, "Disclosing the Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)") state that if authors used AIGC tools (e.g. ChatGPT/LLMs) to develop any portion of a manuscript, use must be disclosed transparently and in detail in the Methods section, pointing to Wiley's publisher-wide Best Practice Guidelines on Research Integrity and Publishing Ethics for full policy. No Bioethics-specific restriction beyond disclosure was found (e.g. no statement banning AI use in idea generation or limiting it to language editing) — journal page just links out to the generic Wiley policy. Wiley's general policy (found via search summary, not directly fetched due to a 402 paywall block on authors.wiley.com) bars listing AI as author/co-author and requires disclosure; permits use for language/grammar, structural clarity, idea development, literature search assistance with transparent disclosure — hence scored as conditional/moderate leniency rather than strict ban or fully open. |
| **Source URL** | https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14678519/homepage/forauthors.html |

### Preprint Policy

> AI-research note (not broken down per-stage): Governed by Wiley's general publisher-wide preprint policy (not a journal-specific statement found on the Bioethics author guidelines page): preprints on non-commercial servers (arXiv, bioRxiv, psyArXiv, SocArXiv, engrXiv etc.) are permitted and submission of a manuscript previously posted as a preprint does not preclude review; authors retain copyright and are advised to use "no re-use" licenses when posting preprints.
> Source: https://authors.wiley.com/author-resources/Journal-Authors/open-access/preprints-policy.html

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Continues to publish traditional analytic/normative bioethics papers on ethics of biomedical and life-science issues (research ethics, public health, genomics, stem cells, organ transplants, ageing) alongside a rapidly growing stream of AI-in-healthcare ethics papers. Recent 2025-2026 examples found: "Artificial Intelligence and Understanding in Medicine" (Adams, Vol 40, 2026) and "Assisting, Replicating, or Autonomously Acting? An Ethical Framework for Integrating AI Tools and Technologies in Healthcare" (Padela et al., Vol 40, 2026), indicating AI-in-medicine ethics is a currently welcomed and active topic area. No dedicated 2026 special-issue CFP was located for this journal specifically (searches surfaced CFPs for sibling/competitor journals like Journal of Bioethical Inquiry and Developing World Bioethics, not for Bioethics itself).

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** Conceptual/normative philosophical analysis, Legal and policy analysis paired with ethical analysis (Health/Law Policy section), Empirical bioethics (mixed-methods integrating data collection with normative argument), Background Briefings (survey-style pieces on current debates)
